refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: Mat is the equivalent in Scilab of the OpenCV type of same name Mat.

When a function outputs an image (such as imread for example), internally OpenCV allocates a Mat object, and a Scilab Mat object is returned, containing a reference to the underlying OpenCV Mat object.
Therefore a Scilab Mat object is not a Scilab matrix (it is a mlist), but it can be manipulated so. The following operators are (or will be) available:

itemizedlist.member: extraction: syntax is the same a the usual Scilab extraction, and returns a Scilab matrix, which type depends on the image type, see details below.
insertion: syntax is the same a the usual Scilab insertion, and accepts a Scilab matrix in input (not yet available).
concatenation: syntax is the same a the usual Scilab concatenation (not yet available).

refsection.para: The full extraction (:) is the only one available operator for the moment. The whole image is returned as a Scilab matrix (if the image has a single channel) or a hypermatrix (one matrix for each channel if the image has several channels, such as a RGB image). Note: OpenCV stores the RBG channels in reverse order, but Scilab rearranges in the standard order.
There are many functions available for the Mat type. Following is a very small list:

itemizedlist.member: constructor: new_Mat() to create a new Mat object. There are several forms of this function, specifying for example the dimensions of the new image, etc.
destructor: delete_Mat() to destroy an existing Mat object. Scilab does not manage the life cycle of Mat objects, they have to be destroyed manually.
Mat_empty() to check an image is not empty. It is very useful since imread does not throw errors when it cannot find an image, but returns an empty image.
Mat_rows_get() and Mat_cols_get() to get rows and columns of the image.
getImageType() to get a string (formated with the OpenCV convention CV_<pixel type>C<number of channels>) giving informations on the type of pixel, or the number of channels of the image.

refsection.para: Note: functions getting as input Mat objects accept also Scilab matrixes, conversion to Mat is automatically done by Scilab.
